findings.element: "Run reconciliation" primary button in its disabled state, with the "Upload file *" blocks below it
findings.finding: When the run is blocked the only clue anywhere on screen is a bare asterisk on "Upload file *" — the greyed-out button carries no tooltip, no list of what is missing, and no highlight on the empty block, and the same dead state appears with no explanation at all when I pick PayPal and the automatic option silently vanishes.
findings.user_impact: I click the main button, nothing happens, nothing tells me which of the three boxes I still owe you, and this is exactly the point where I close the tab and go back to the tool my accountant uses.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the blocker in plain words next to the button — e.g. "Add the Balance change file to start" — and when an integration has no automatic option, say so where the option used to be: "PayPal can't be retrieved automatically. Upload the two files below."

evidence.source: plain-language — vocabulary.md "### Validation — Default: `Required`" gives a validation word but nothing on screen states which item is required; a disabled primary action with no named precondition is unexplained (KF-9)

findings.element: "Import method" dropdown on the Integration card — the "Assisted" option
findings.finding: "Assisted" sits between "Automated (recommended)" and "Manual" with no description of what it is or who does the assisting, and picking it asks me for 2 files where "Manual" only asks for 1 — so the middle option is more work than the manual one, which is the opposite of what the name suggests.
findings.user_impact: I assume "Assisted" means Synder helps me so it must be the easier of the two, pick it, and end up hunting for a second report I was never told I needed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one line of helper text under the dropdown that says what each option asks of me — e.g. "Assisted — you download 2 reports from Stripe, we do the rest" — or rename it to describe the work, such as "I'll upload the reports".

evidence.source: unexplained jargon — not a term in vocabulary.md; no on-screen definition, and the label contradicts the amount of work it requires

findings.element: "Account to reconcile" hint, warning state after picking "Stripe fees" or "Stripe sales"
findings.finding: The warning uses "connections" — a word that appears nowhere else on this screen, where the same thing is labelled "Integration" — never names which account I should pick instead, hedges with "may not know", and leaves "Run reconciliation" fully enabled so I cannot tell whether I have made a real mistake or not.
findings.user_impact: I do not know whether I have just broken something or been given a footnote, I cannot tell what "the account tied to this connection" is, and because the button still works I proceed on the wrong account — the currency confirmation I had a moment ago has also disappeared from that same line.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the account and keep the currency: "Use Stripe mzkt.by (USD) — Stripe fees is also used by other integrations, so results may be wrong," and say plainly whether I can still run it.

evidence.quote: Stripe fees is shared across connections, so Synder may not know which one to use. Prefer the account tied to this connection.
evidence.source: vocabulary.md UI Words: "| **Integration** | payment platform, sales platform, provider, system |" — "connections" is not the canonical term, and the screen labels the same control "Integration"

gaps: Upload blocks: no real file input exists — Browse fabricates "General_ledger_export_export.csv" — so wrong-file-type, oversized-file and parse-failure copy was never reached and cannot be checked for whether it names what went wrong.

Automatic retrieval: failure and empty-result states are not implemented, so the copy a user sees when the retrieval that was "Recommended" fails is unknown — this is the exact place a generic message would be a dead end.

After "Run reconciliation": the prototype ends at the "Reconciliation started" status and no results view is built, so whether a non-expert ever learns what reconciliation produced, and whether it is presented as undoable, is untested.
Close (✕): clicking it produces no dialog and no navigation, so the discard-confirmation copy — whether I am warned that leaving loses my setup — was never exercised.
Custom date range: no validation of any kind fires for an end-before-start or an all-future range, so there is no error copy to evaluate.
